findings.title: Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing
findings.body: The code passes a negative `start_offset` to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`. Django QuerySets explicitly raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` when sliced with negative indices. The comment claiming 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false. This will crash at runtime for any request that triggers this code path with a negative offset.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key cannot handle datetime fields
findings.body: The endpoint uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `self.key` is `"datetime"` and `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a Python `datetime` object. The `get_item_key` method then calls `math.floor(value)` or `math.ceil(value)` on it, which raises `TypeError`. The existing `DateTimePaginator` correctly converts the datetime to a numeric value first via `float(value.strftime("%s.%f")) * self.multiplier`. This paginator is a copy of the numeric `Paginator` and is incompatible with datetime fields.

findings.title: BasePaginator.get_result behavior changed for all subclasses
findings.body: The change from `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` modifies the base class used by `Paginator`, `DateTimePaginator`, and all other subclasses. When `cursor.is_prev` is False, negative offsets are now silently clamped to 0 instead of being passed through (which would have raised an error from Django). While this may be defensively safe, it silently changes error behavior for all existing paginators and could mask bugs in callers that incorrectly produce negative offsets.

findings.title: enable_advanced_features kwarg may not reach the paginator constructor
findings.body: The `self.paginate()` helper in Sentry's base endpoint typically accepts a fixed set of parameters (request, queryset, paginator_cls, order_by, on_results, etc.) and constructs the paginator internally. Passing `enable_advanced_features=True` as an extra keyword argument will either be silently ignored (if `self.paginate` uses `**kwargs` but doesn't forward them) or raise a TypeError. If it's silently ignored, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` will be instantiated with `enable_advanced_features=False` (the default), making the 'advanced' code path unreachable.

findings.title: Authorization check uses organization_context.member without null check
findings.body: The expression `organization_context.member.has_global_access` will raise `AttributeError` if `organization_context.member` is None. Depending on how the endpoint is invoked and what authentication states are possible, this could result in a 500 error rather than a proper 403. The `OrganizationAuditPermission` may guarantee a member exists, but this is fragile and not explicitly defended here.

findings.title: Misleading comment added without corresponding code change
findings.body: The comment 'Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios' is added to `Cursor.__init__`, but the code `self.offset = int(offset)` already accepted any integer including negative values before this PR. The comment implies a behavioral change was made here, but no actual validation was removed or added. This is misleading for future maintainers and the real (broken) negative offset handling is in the paginator, not here.
